meta.title: Terraform Factory Modules: Verify Before You Depend

views.label: A search turns up a candidate
views.note: GitHub's activity feed and star count are not proof of a maintained module.

views.label: Two traps look fine at a glance
views.note: One looks active from issues/PRs alone; one forbids the fork everyone assumes is allowed.

views.label: Cite, automate, or skip
views.note: Only a maintained, permissively-licensed, cleanly-shaped module is worth automating against.

cards.title: Two real traps
items: A repo can show recent stars/issues/PRs with zero commits merged to main in over a year
A repo can compose genuinely well-shaped modules under a license that forbids modifying them
Both pass a casual GitHub-page glance -- neither passes reading pushed_at and LICENSE directly

cards.title: Verification order matters
items: Commit date first -- staleness alone rules out most candidates
License second -- a stale-but-permissive module can still be pinned and used as-is
Input shape last -- only worth reading source once the first two gates pass

cards.title: Automation is the rare outcome
items: Most candidates end at 'cite with caveats', not 'automate'
Only a maintained module with a clean list-driven shape justifies new dbxmig code
Forcing automation onto a stale or narrow shape means maintaining someone else's schema drift
